title: Immunogenicity and Safety of AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 Influenza Vaccine in Children 6-35 Months of Age: Results From a Phase 2, Randomized, Observer-blind, Multicenter, Dose-ranging Study.
ehr_evidence: The study was a phase 2 randomized, multicenter, observer-blind, dose-ranging clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02719743); data were collected prospectively through clinical trial procedures including blood sampling for serologic assays and adverse-event recording, not from electronic health records.
summary: A phase 2 randomized, observer-blind, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial evaluated immunogenicity and safety of five formulations of AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 influenza vaccine in 185 healthy children 6–35 months of age in Thailand and Taiwan.
key_findings: All formulations elicited strong homologous immune responses with all subjects' hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers ≥1:40 post-vaccination (SCR = 100%, SPR = 100%).
The 1.9 µg HA/AS03B formulation ranked highest on the immunogenicity-fever index based on HI and microneutralization (MN) assays.
Antibody levels persisted >4 times above baseline 12 months after primary vaccination (day 385) with all formulations (SPR >70%, SCR >40%, MGI Day 385/Day 0 >4).
Antibodies increased >4-fold after antigen challenge (day 392/day 385); VRR was 100% for all formulations at day 392.
Overall per-subject incidence of fever ranged from 28.6% (3.75 µg HA/AS03D) to 60.5% (1.9 µg HA/AS03B); grade 3 fever (≥39.0°C) occurred in 18.4% of 1.9 µg HA/AS03B.
Serious adverse events were reported in 29 subjects (15.7%); none were fatal or related to vaccination, and no safety signal was identified.
No vaccine-specific CD8+ T-cell response was detected with any formulation.
captured_features: Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) titers, GMT, seroprotection rate (SPR), seroconversion rate (SCR), mean geometric increase (MGI)
Microneutralization (MN) titers, GMT, vaccine response rate (VRR)
Solicited and unsolicited adverse events, medically attended AEs, AESIs, serious AEs
pathologies_diseases: Kawasaki disease (one reported immune-mediated event, assessed as unrelated to vaccine)
study_design: Phase 2 randomized, observer-blind, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial (no placebo control)
data_source_type: biospecimen (clinical trial with serologic assays and adverse-event collection)
population: 185 healthy children 6–35 months of age (male and female) at 7 centers in Thailand and Taiwan
limitations: Absence of a placebo control limits the ability to assess vaccine safety and generalizability.
The immunogenicity-fever index did not include other reactogenicity indicators such as drowsiness and loss of appetite, using fever alone as a proxy.
